summary: A Netlify support forum thread where CongChuong reports that a Vite React project builds locally but fails on Netlify with a Rollup error 'Could not resolve ./Pages/Home/Home from src/App.jsx'. Forum member hrishikesh points to a Netlify support guide on case sensitivity, and later identifies the cause: the import uses an uppercase 'P' in 'Pages' while the GitHub repo folder is lowercase 'pages'. The thread shows the build log and the case-sensitivity fix.
one_line: Forum thread where a Vite React app fails on Netlify with a missing-import error, caused by a case mismatch in the 'Pages' folder name.
key_facts: CongChuong reported on August 5, 2023 that a Netlify build of a React project built with Vite fails with 'Could not resolve ./Pages/Home/Home from src/App.jsx'.
The project runs fine on localhost but fails on Netlify during the 'building site' stage.
The build log shows 'vite v4.4.8 building for production...' followed by 'RollupError: Could not resolve ./Pages/Home/Home from src/App.jsx'.
The Netlify build command was 'CI='' npm run build' and the publish directory was /opt/build/repo/Client/dist.
The build ran in the directory /opt/build/repo/Client, with @netlify/build version 29.17.4.
hrishikesh replied on August 5, 2023 with a link to a Netlify support guide on case sensitivity, which says case issues often cause files to be missing on Netlify but not locally.
CongChuong replied on August 10, 2023 that they had checked carefully and had no case errors in their code.
hrishikesh replied on August 11, 2023 that the error is the uppercase 'P' in './Pages/Home/Home'.
hrishikesh stated that the GitHub repo uses a lowercase 'p' in the folder name.
The Netlify support guide was last reviewed by Netlify Support Staff in December 2022.
